## Frequently asked questions

**What is behavioral therapy for obesity?**

Behavioral therapy for obesity helps you understand and modify your relationship with food through counseling, coping skills, goal setting, and mindful eating. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and movement education in one Intensive Outpatient Program, led by an experienced and compassionate team of behavioral healthcare professionals.

**What does a bariatric psychologist do?**

A bariatric psychologist works with clients on the emotional and behavioral aspects of weight struggles, including binge eating, emotional eating, and chronic overeating. Our clinical psychologist and licensed professional counselors provide therapy focused on recovery and coping skills, intuitive eating, and family engagement, helping clients build sustainable habits and a healthier relationship with food.

**What does a bariatric dietitian do?**

A bariatric dietitian provides nutritional education, meal planning, and practical support tailored to your needs. Our registered dietitians lead grocery store tours, teach you how to navigate dining out, and work alongside our professional chef in cooking classes. We focus on sustainable dietary changes that fit your life, not rigid rules or restrictive meal plans.

**What therapy is best for weight loss?**

The most effective therapy addresses the behavioral and emotional patterns behind overeating. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we combine behavioral therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and movement education in one program. This comprehensive approach, delivered by healthcare professionals in four disciplines, helps clients build lasting skills. One program, not four.

**What is the mental health evaluation for bariatric surgery?**

Most bariatric surgery programs require a psychological evaluation to assess readiness and identify any behavioral or emotional factors that may affect outcomes. If you are preparing for surgery or already had it, our Intensive Outpatient Program can provide the behavioral support you need. Your surgeon decides the medical requirements, and we coordinate care with your medical providers throughout treatment.

If you have questions about our program or would like to learn more, we invite you to reach out.

## Frequently asked questions

**How can I train my brain to stop overeating?**

We help clients understand and modify their relationship with food through behavioral therapy, mindful eating education, and dietary guidance from registered dietitians. Our Intensive Outpatient Program teaches recovery and coping skills you can use long after treatment ends. A licensed therapist can work with you on the specific thoughts and behaviors driving overeating.

**How do I stop my cravings and overeating?**

Stopping cravings and overeating takes more than willpower. We provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and mindful eating education in one program. Our team helps clients build coping skills, set realistic goals, and create a sustainable plan. You work with a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, and registered dietitians who understand the behavioral side of food.

**Why do people binge?**

Binge eating has many causes, including emotional triggers, stress, past dieting, and the way our brains respond to certain foods. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we focus on understanding those patterns and learning new ways to cope. Our behavioral therapy and counseling help clients address the underlying reasons they turn to food, not just the eating itself.

**Where does binge eating start?**

Binge eating often starts with a combination of emotional, environmental, and biological factors. It can develop after years of dieting, during stressful life events, or as a way to manage difficult feelings. We help clients trace those patterns and build healthier responses. A licensed therapist or psychologist is the right person to explore your individual history and triggers.

If you are struggling with binge eating or chronic overeating, we are here to help. Reach out to learn more about our program.

OA meetings offer peer support and community, which many people find valuable. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we complement that approach with professional clinical care: licensed therapists, registered dietitians, cooking classes and movement education in one program. We work with people who attend OA, people who have tried it, and people exploring other paths.

**What is overeating a symptom of?**

Overeating can be tied to stress, anxiety, depression, binge eating disorder, or learned patterns around food. A licensed therapist or psychologist is the right person to explore what is driving it in your specific situation. We help clients understand and modify their relationship with food through behavioral therapy, dietary guidance and coping skills.

**What is the easiest way to stop overeating?**

There is no single easy fix, but understanding the emotional and behavioral patterns behind overeating is a strong foundation. We teach coping skills, mindful eating, nutritional planning and goal setting in group and individual therapy. Recovery takes time, and we provide structured support over roughly three months and 30 sessions in our Intensive Outpatient Program.

**What are the controversies surrounding Overeaters Anonymous?**

Some people appreciate OA's spiritual foundation and 12-step structure. Others prefer a clinical, evidence-based approach with licensed professionals. At BCC, we respect all pathways and do not replace OA. We offer comprehensive behavioral healthcare that can stand alone or work alongside peer support groups, depending on what fits your needs.

If you are looking for professional support for overeating, we are here to help. Reach out to learn more about our program.

If you find yourself struggling with overeating, reaching out for professional support is a good first step. Changing patterns around food takes more than willpower. It involves learning new coping skills, understanding emotional triggers, and building sustainable habits. Our therapists and dietitians work with clients on mindful eating, goal setting, and practical strategies that make lasting change possible. We teach these skills in both individual sessions and group settings, so you have ongoing support as you build new patterns.

Binge eating often stems from a combination of emotional, behavioral, and environmental factors. There is rarely just one cause. We work on these issues through individual therapy, group support, and practical education around food, nutrition, and mindful eating in our Intensive Outpatient Program.
